## Load all packages
```{r}

library("rlang")
library("Seurat");
library("sctransform");
library("dplyr");
library("RColorBrewer");
library("ggthemes");
library("ggplot2");
library("cowplot");
library("data.table");
library("scales")


```


## Set up Seurat object
```{r}

memory.limit(size=50000000)

samples=c("xu43","xu48")

data.10x = list()

data.10x[[1]] <- Read10X(data.dir = "xu43_FM/raw_feature_bc_matrix");

data.10x[[2]] <- Read10X(data.dir = "xu48_FM/raw_feature_bc_matrix");



setwd("C:/Users/Xiaosa Xu/Desktop/Cross-organ-meristem-SC/FM")


## Convert each feature-barcode matrix to a Seurat object.

FM.list = list(); 

FM.list[[1]] = CreateSeuratObject(counts = data.10x[[1]], min.cells=3, min.features=200, project=samples[1]);

FM.list[[1]][["DataSet"]] = samples[1];

FM.list[[2]] = CreateSeuratObject(counts = data.10x[[2]], min.cells=3, min.features=200, project=samples[2]);

FM.list[[2]][["DataSet"]] = samples[2];


### Subset each library before merge or integrate


FM.list[[1]] <- subset(FM.list[[1]], subset = nCount_RNA > 5000 & nFeature_RNA > 1000 & nCount_RNA < 150000 & nFeature_RNA < 15000)

FM.list[[2]] <- subset(FM.list[[2]], subset = nCount_RNA > 5000 & nFeature_RNA > 1000 & nCount_RNA < 150000 & nFeature_RNA < 15000)


## logNormalize

FM.list[[1]]<- NormalizeData(FM.list[[1]], normalization.method = "LogNormalize", scale.factor = 10000)

FM.list[[2]]<- NormalizeData(FM.list[[2]], normalization.method = "LogNormalize", scale.factor = 10000)


##Find variables


FM.list[[1]]<- FindVariableFeatures(FM.list[[1]], selection.method = "vst", nfeatures = 2000)

FM.list[[2]]<- FindVariableFeatures(FM.list[[2]], selection.method = "vst", nfeatures = 2000)


# select features that are repeatedly variable across datasets for integration


features <- SelectIntegrationFeatures(object.list = FM.list)


# find anchors

anchors <- FindIntegrationAnchors(object.list = FM.list, anchor.features = features)


# Integrate data
# this command creates an 'integrated' data assay

FM.int <- IntegrateData(anchorset = anchors)


DefaultAssay(FM.int)<-"integrated"


# Run the standard workflow for visualization and clustering
FM.int <- ScaleData(FM.int, verbose = FALSE)
FM.int <- RunPCA(FM.int, npcs = 30, verbose = FALSE)


ElbowPlot(FM.int, ndims = 40)

## Elbow plot: quantitative approach
## https://hbctraining.github.io/scRNA-seq/lessons/elbow_plot_metric.html

# Determine percent of variation associated with each PC
pct <- FM.int[["pca"]]@stdev / sum(FM.int[["pca"]]@stdev) * 100

# Calculate cumulative percents for each PC
cumu <- cumsum(pct)

# Determine which PC exhibits cumulative percent greater than 90% and % variation associated with the PC as less than 5
co1 <- which(cumu > 90 & pct < 5)[1]

co1


# Determine the difference between variation of PC and subsequent PC
co2 <- sort(which((pct[1:length(pct) - 1] - pct[2:length(pct)]) > 0.1), decreasing = T)[1] + 1

# last point where change of % of variation is more than 0.1%.
co2


# Minimum of the two calculation
pcs <- min(co1, co2)

pcs

```



```{r}
FM.int <- RunUMAP(FM.int, reduction = "pca", dims = 1:pcs) ## PC number based on above Elbow plot: quantitative approach

FM.int <- FindNeighbors(FM.int, reduction = "pca", dims = 1:pcs)

FM.int <- FindClusters(FM.int, resolution = 0.8)

# Visualization

DimPlot(FM.int, reduction = "umap", label = TRUE, pt.size = 1)
DimPlot(FM.int, reduction = "umap", group.by = "orig.ident")

## two plots next to each other 

p1 <- DimPlot(FM.int, reduction = "umap", group.by = "orig.ident", pt.size = 1)
p2 <- DimPlot(FM.int, reduction = "umap", label = TRUE, repel = TRUE, pt.size = 1, label.size = 10)
p1 + p2

### split the UMAPs by samples 

DimPlot(FM.int, reduction = "umap", split.by = "orig.ident", pt.size = 1)


### group the UMAPs by samples. 

DimPlot(FM.int, reduction = "umap", group.by = "orig.ident", pt.size = 1)

```

```{r}
## save 

saveRDS(FM.int, file = "FM.int.rds")


```


```{r}
## Remove cluster with low UMI or doublet

FM.int_rmDB <- subset(FM.int, idents = c("10"), invert = TRUE)

DimPlot(FM.int_rmDB, reduction = "umap", label = TRUE, pt.size = 1)


### split the integrated object to re-normalize and process

FM_int.rmDB.recluster.list <- SplitObject(FM.int_rmDB, split.by = "orig.ident")

FM_int.rmDB.recluster.list


DefaultAssay(FM_int.rmDB.recluster.list[[1]]) <- "RNA"
DefaultAssay(FM_int.rmDB.recluster.list[[2]]) <- "RNA"


## logNormalize

FM_int.rmDB.recluster.list[[1]]<- NormalizeData(FM_int.rmDB.recluster.list[[1]], normalization.method = "LogNormalize", scale.factor = 10000)

FM_int.rmDB.recluster.list[[2]]<- NormalizeData(FM_int.rmDB.recluster.list[[2]], normalization.method = "LogNormalize", scale.factor = 10000)


## Find variables


FM_int.rmDB.recluster.list[[1]]<- FindVariableFeatures(FM_int.rmDB.recluster.list[[1]], selection.method = "vst", nfeatures = 2000)

FM_int.rmDB.recluster.list[[2]]<- FindVariableFeatures(FM_int.rmDB.recluster.list[[2]], selection.method = "vst", nfeatures = 2000)


# select features that are repeatedly variable across datasets for integration


features <- SelectIntegrationFeatures(object.list = FM_int.rmDB.recluster.list)


# find anchors

anchors <- FindIntegrationAnchors(object.list = FM_int.rmDB.recluster.list, anchor.features = features)


# Integrate data
# this command creates an 'integrated' data assay

FM_int.rmDB.recluster.int <- IntegrateData(anchorset = anchors)


DefaultAssay(FM_int.rmDB.recluster.int)<-"integrated"


# Run the standard workflow for visualization and clustering
FM_int.rmDB.recluster.int <- ScaleData(FM_int.rmDB.recluster.int, verbose = FALSE)
FM_int.rmDB.recluster.int <- RunPCA(FM_int.rmDB.recluster.int, npcs = 30, verbose = FALSE)


## Determine the ‘dimensionality’ of the dataset

ElbowPlot(FM_int.rmDB.recluster.int, ndims = 40)

## Elbow plot: quantitative approach
## https://hbctraining.github.io/scRNA-seq/lessons/elbow_plot_metric.html

# Determine percent of variation associated with each PC
pct <- FM_int.rmDB.recluster.int[["pca"]]@stdev / sum(FM_int.rmDB.recluster.int[["pca"]]@stdev) * 100

# Calculate cumulative percents for each PC
cumu <- cumsum(pct)

# Determine which PC exhibits cumulative percent greater than 90% and % variation associated with the PC as less than 5
co1 <- which(cumu > 90 & pct < 5)[1]

co1

# Determine the difference between variation of PC and subsequent PC
co2 <- sort(which((pct[1:length(pct) - 1] - pct[2:length(pct)]) > 0.1), decreasing = T)[1] + 1

# last point where change of % of variation is more than 0.1%.
co2

# Minimum of the two calculation
pcs <- min(co1, co2)

pcs


```

```{r}
## transfer the subcluster10 labels to be active labels.

subcluster.base_periphery.epi <- ScaleData(subcluster.base_periphery.epi, verbose = FALSE)

subcluster.base_periphery.epi <- RunPCA(subcluster.base_periphery.epi, npcs = 30, verbose = FALSE)


ElbowPlot(subcluster.base_periphery.epi, ndims = 40)

## Elbow plot: quantitative approach
## https://hbctraining.github.io/scRNA-seq/lessons/elbow_plot_metric.html

# Determine percent of variation associated with each PC
pct <- subcluster.base_periphery.epi[["pca"]]@stdev / sum(subcluster.base_periphery.epi[["pca"]]@stdev) * 100

# Calculate cumulative percents for each PC
cumu <- cumsum(pct)

# Determine which PC exhibits cumulative percent greater than 90% and % variation associated with the PC as less than 5
co1 <- which(cumu > 90 & pct < 5)[1]

co1


# Determine the difference between variation of PC and subsequent PC
co2 <- sort(which((pct[1:length(pct) - 1] - pct[2:length(pct)]) > 0.1), decreasing = T)[1] + 1

# last point where change of % of variation is more than 0.1%.
co2


# Minimum of the two calculation
pcs <- min(co1, co2)

pcs



subcluster.base_periphery.epi <- RunUMAP(subcluster.base_periphery.epi, reduction = "pca", dims = 1:pcs) ## Use PC number based on above Elbow plot: quantitative approach

subcluster.base_periphery.epi <- FindNeighbors(subcluster.base_periphery.epi, reduction = "pca", dims = 1:pcs)

subcluster.base_periphery.epi <- FindClusters(subcluster.base_periphery.epi, resolution = 0.2)
```

```{r}

library(Seurat)

## 1) load the already-annotated object
FM.final <- readRDS("FM.final.rds")

## 2) final cluster colors (taken from  FM DimPlot; only labels used in FM)
cluster.colors <- c(
  "Cortex"="#afbca5","Pith"="#99b6ca",
  "S.Phase.(non.epi.I)"="#D4D915","S.Phase.(non.epi.II)"="#95511f","S.Phase.(non.epi.III)"="#00A9FF",
  "S.Phase.(epi)"="#e9967a",
  "G2.M.Phase.(non.epi.I)"="#737172","G2.M.Phase.(non.epi.II)"="#e761d8","G2.M.Phase.(non.epi.III)"="#28CECA",
  "G2.M.Phase.(epi)"="#808000",
  "Determinate.Lateral.Organ.(epi)"="#98fb98","Determinate.Lateral.Organ.(non.epi)"="#64ac4e",
  "Meristem.Tip.non.epi.(stem.cell)"="#e93f33","Meristem.Tip.epi.(stem.cell)"="#F68282",
  "Meristem.Boundary"="#1FA195","Vasculature"="#ffa500")

## 3) check that the saved identities match the color names
cur <- as.character(Idents(FM.final))
print(table(cur))
missing <- setdiff(unique(cur), names(cluster.colors))
if (length(missing) > 0) stop("These labels have no color: ", paste(missing, collapse = ", "))

## 4) set identity levels in color order
Idents(FM.final) <- factor(cur, levels = names(cluster.colors)[names(cluster.colors) %in% cur])

## 5) store labels, per-cell colors, and the palette in the object
FM.final$final_annotation <- as.character(Idents(FM.final))
FM.final$final_color <- unname(cluster.colors[FM.final$final_annotation])
FM.final@misc$cluster_colors <- cluster.colors

## 6) check the plot, then save under a new name
DimPlot(FM.final, reduction = "umap", label = TRUE, label.size = 5, pt.size = 1,
        cols = FM.final@misc$cluster_colors)

saveRDS(FM.final, file = "FM.final.updated.color.rds")

```
